title: Collections policy spec

stage.description: Call stage: opening (before the person is confirmed), third_party (someone else answered), identity (security questions), negotiate (after verification: debt, promise, confirmation), any (every stage).

source_ref.description: Where in the brief: e.g. "rule 4", "memo of <date>", or a list of them.

rule.description: nth_business_day: the n-th business day after today. calendar_days: today + n calendar days. end_of_month: last day of the current month. end_of_next_month: last day of next month. fixed_weekday_after_n_weeks: the given weekday (0=Monday) of this week, plus `weeks` weeks.

snap.description: If the computed day is not a business day: back = previous business day, forward = next business day, null/absent = keep it.

deadline_rule.description: How the promise deadline is computed from today (the date part of `now`).

amount.description: current: the full past-due amount, or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much. full: always the full past-due amount. floor: the floor amount (products[type].floor_field).

date.description: today. last_business_day_of_week: the last business day of this week, or of next week if today is that day. deadline: the band deadline. next_business_day: the business day after today. Always capped at the deadline.

attempt.description: One persuasion attempt: which amount, on which date.

bank_name.description: The organisation name as said to the customer (bank, insurer, ...).

assistant_identity.description: What the agent says it is, e.g. when asked whether it is a robot.

address_as.description: How to address the customer, as a template over call_variables, e.g. "{<honorific_var>} {<surname_var>}".

call_variables.description: Names of the variables every call starts with (the brief's call-variable table).

first_sentence.description: The first sentence, said word for word. Must contain every fact the brief requires in it.

confirm_question.description: The question that confirms the customer, said word for word.

confirm_reject.description: Answers that do NOT count as confirmation (ask again).

max_asks.description: How many times the confirm question may be asked in total before closing with the unclear event.

banned_before_verify.description: Words or topics never said before identity is verified (to anyone).

opening.description: The first turns, before the person on the line is confirmed as the customer.

say_nothing_beyond_opening.description: True: say nothing about the reason for the call beyond the opening sentence.

days.description: Which days a callback may be booked on.

inclusive.description: Whether `from` and `to` themselves are allowed. Default when absent: true (both included).

after_now.description: True: the callback must be later than `now`.

window_retries.description: How many more times to ask for another time when the offered one is outside the window.

fixed_sentences.description: Sentences said word for word, keyed by event id (e.g. deceased).

third_party.description: When someone other than the customer answers.

ask.description: The question, said word for word.

format.description: date: send as YYYY-MM-DD. digits: exactly `length` digits. year: a four-digit year from 1900 to the current year. text: as said.

date_order.description: How to read a date given only as numbers (DMY = day, month, year).

length.description: Number of digits for format digits.

max_wrong.description: Wrong answers that end the check.

wrong_scope.description: total: counted across all questions. per_question: counted per question.

non_counting_hints.description: verify_identity hint value -> what to ask instead. These retries are not wrong answers.

decline_explanation.description: Said (once) when the customer does not want to answer.

decline_limit.description: The n-th refusal (or 'what is this about' instead of an answer) closes with the declined event.

failed_advice.description: Said after the check fails, before closing.

identity.description: Security questions, asked in order, each checked with verify_identity.

calendar.description: Business days used by every date rule.

words.description: How the product is said, may use product fields, e.g. "<product noun> ending {<id_field>}".

floor_field.description: The get_account product field that holds the floor (lowest acceptable amount).

amount_field.description: The get_account product field that holds the full overdue amount. Default when absent: past_due. Sentences still say {past_due}.

days_late_field.description: The get_account product field that holds how many days the payment is late. Default when absent: days_late. Sentences still say {days_late}.

products.description: Keyed by get_account product `type`. Every openapi product type needs an entry.

name.description: The band's name from the brief.

attempts.description: Persuasion attempts in order; their count is the number of attempts allowed.

bands.description: days_late ranges, contiguous with no gap or overlap. Each sets the deadline rule and the persuasion attempts.

debt_statement.description: The debt statement for one product, said after verification.

first_ask.description: The first ask for payment, said word for word.

times.description: How many times the floor may be offered.

sentence_suffix.description: Sentence added to the floor offer, word for word.

floor_offer.description: Offering the floor when the full amount is too much.

below_floor.description: When the customer proposes less than the floor.

vague_date.description: When the customer gives a vague period instead of a day.

weekday_words.description: Meaning of "next <weekday>" and "this <weekday>". following_week: that weekday in the next calendar week.

non_business_day.description: When the customer names a weekend day or holiday on or before the deadline.

after_deadline.description: When the customer names a date after the deadline.

never_ask_how_much.description: True: the agent proposes every amount and never asks how much the customer can pay.

debt_statement_per_product.description: Optional, multi-product briefs: one sentence per late product, said for each product in order, after a lead-in. Absent: use debt_statement for each.

first_ask_all.description: Optional, multi-product briefs: the first ask covering every product at once, said word for word when the brief quotes it. Absent: first_ask is used.

negotiation.description: Stating the debt and getting a promise.

id.description: Event id; also referenced by outcomes[].event and by path selectors events[<id>].

trigger.description: When it fires, in plain words (used for intent detection).

stages.description: Stages in which the trigger is listened for.

say.description: A sentence said WORD FOR WORD when the event fires, or null. Only put exact brief wording here.

instruction.description: Guidance for the dialogue model, NOT said verbatim (e.g. 'acknowledge briefly', 'stay neutral').

action.description: close: close the call with outcome/reason. transfer: transfer_to_agent(queue), then close with outcome/reason. insist_once_then_transfer: ask once whether you can help first (say); transfer only if the customer insists. offer_transfer_else_close: offer a transfer; accepted -> transfer to queue and close with outcome/reason, declined -> close with else_outcome/else_reason. note_and_continue (multi-product): note per_product_note on the current product and continue with the next; outcome/reason are used if the call ends on it.

queue.description: transfer_to_agent queue enum value; required for the transfer actions.

outcome.description: close_call outcome (openapi enum) for this event, or null.

reason.description: close_call reason, or null (only for outcomes the openapi says take no reason).

else_outcome.description: offer_transfer_else_close only: close_call outcome when the transfer is declined.

else_reason.description: offer_transfer_else_close only: close_call reason when the transfer is declined.

times.description: How many times the trigger must occur before the event fires. Default when absent: 1.

overrides_persuasion.description: True: once this fires, no persuasion attempt is made, and it takes precedence over the attempts ladder and other negotiation events.

per_product_note.description: add_note reason to record on the product(s) concerned when notes are enabled, or null.

events.description: Customer situations that change the call's course. Known ids map to fixed graph branches (promise_recorded, paid, dispute, restructuring, human, hardship, refused, service_error, failed, declined, callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased, unclear, not_talk); other ids become generic intent branches.

say.description: The sentence, said word for word.

stages.description: Stages where the rule applies. Default when absent: ["any"].

say_rules.description: Fixed answers that do not change the call's course: say the sentence, then continue.

question.description: Asked after reading back product, amount and date, word for word.

retries.description: Extra create_promise attempts after a failure (1 = try once more).

success_sentence.description: Said word for word after create_promise returns ok: true.

failure_event.description: Event id fired when create_promise still fails after the retries.

change_note.description: Said when the customer asks to change a recorded promise, or null.

order.description: Order the products are discussed in.

ask_all_today_first.description: True: first ask whether all products can be paid today, then go product by product.

single_readback.description: True: read every promise back together and ask one confirmation.

shared_date_after_deadline.description: One date named for all products that is past one product's deadline.

enabled.description: False when the brief never uses add_note.

reasons.description: Allowed add_note reasons (subset of the openapi enum).

on_transfer.description: none: no notes at all on a call that is transferred (before or after it).

timing.description: When add_note is called. immediate: as soon as a product ends without a promise. at_close: notes are collected and written only just before a non-transfer close_call, so a later transfer leaves no notes. Default when absent: immediate.

notes.description: add_note policy for products that end without a promise.

no_promise_reason.description: first_non_paid_note: with no promise, close no_promise with the reason of the first product (in order) whose note is not paid.

all_paid_outcome.description: close_call outcome when every product is noted paid and no promise was recorded.

multi_product.description: How a call with several late products is run. Present for single-product briefs too (notes disabled).

thank_and_goodbye.description: True: thank the customer and say goodbye before close_call.

reason.description: close_call reason; null only for promise and paid.

outcomes.description: The brief's outcome table: each (outcome, reason) pair and the event that produces it.

unused_outcomes.description: Optional: openapi close_call outcomes the brief never uses.

instruction.description: How the agent gets the value from the customer (when to ask, what to do when the answer fits no allowed value). Not said verbatim.

default.description: Value sent when the customer gives none that fits (an openapi enum value when the field has an enum), or null.

value.description: A fixed value the brief sets for every call: sent as is, never asked.

tool_fields.description: Optional: request fields of an openapi tool that the compiler has no slot for, keyed "<tool>.<field>" (e.g. a required create_promise field beyond product_id, amount and date). Every such required field is sent; this says how to fill it.

extra_rules.description: Escape hatch: brief rules no structured field expresses, injected into the prompt of the given stage.

custom_code.description: Python function bodies for date or amount rules the enums cannot express, tested by examples.

examples.description: Concrete date vectors checked with builder.lib.dates. deadline: {today, days_late, expect}. attempt: also attempt_index (1-based); expect is that attempt's proposed date.

field.description: A path into the spec: dotted keys plus brackets. A bracket holds a list index (bands[1].deadline.n) or the id of a list item (events[paid].say, events[paid]).

conflicts.description: Decisions on contradictions, overrides or gaps in the brief; field is a spec path.

maps_to.description: A path into the spec: dotted keys plus brackets. A bracket holds a list index (bands[1].deadline.n) or the id of a list item (events[paid].say, events[paid]). Must resolve; extra_rules[n] is allowed.

facts.description: Optional fact pass: every checkable statement in the brief with its quote and where it lives in the spec.

sources.description: Spec path -> brief citation. Keys are paths: A path into the spec: dotted keys plus brackets. A bracket holds a list index (bands[1].deadline.n) or the id of a list item (events[paid].say, events[paid]).

description: Policy spec for one brief (an organisation's collections call policy). Every fact in the brief lives here; the compiler is generic. Sentences use single-brace placeholders {name}: call_variables, get_account product fields, or product_words, past_due, days_late, floor, deadline, amount, date, product.
